sources.title: Raporty klimatyczne dla Polski (Climate reports for Poland)
sources.organization: Institute of Meteorology and Water Management – National Research Institute (IMGW-PIB)
sources.temporal_coverage: National observations for 2025 compared with the 1991–2020 normal.
sources.methodology: Official IMGW-PIB report-entry summary reports national station-network measurements for 2025 against the 1991–2020 normal.
sources.limitations: The linked report PDF was inaccessible; only the publisher summary was read, so no regional breakdown or detailed methods are claimed.

sources.title: Zmiana klimatu w Polsce. Fakty, liczby, skutki
sources.organization: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
sources.temporal_coverage: Temperature trend since 1951; March 2026 conditions; water-availability and European drought statistics reported for recent years including 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry explainer synthesizes climate statistics and consequences, citing IMGW, IOŚ-PIB and Copernicus.
sources.limitations: The page does not reproduce measurement uncertainty, full methods or regional disaggregation for every statistic.

sources.title: Susza w Wielkopolsce. Partnerstwo regionalne
sources.organization: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional water-balance trends described since the beginning of the 21st century; partnership letter signed 2 April 2026; projects reported as in implementation.
sources.methodology: Ministry page summarizes regional drought assessment, partnership and projects.
sources.limitations: No underlying hydrological data or project evaluation is presented.

sources.title: Urban Overheating & Adaptation Measures: An Analysis at EU, National, and Local Level
sources.temporal_coverage: Polish city adaptation-project implementation and reported measures mainly cover 2001–2019; report published in 2024.
sources.methodology: World Bank review includes national policies and Polish city adaptation cases.
sources.limitations: Not an impact evaluation; underlying municipal plans were not inspected.

sources.title: Prime Minister: We will spare no expense rebuilding flooded areas
sources.organization: Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland
geographic_coverage: flood-affected settlements under a state of natural disaster
sources.temporal_coverage: Preliminary flood-impact and evacuation figures presented at a government briefing on 21 September 2024.
sources.methodology: Chancellery statement summarizes preliminary reports supplied by regional governors at the 21 September 2024 crisis meeting.
sources.limitations: Figures were provisional; standing water prevented complete inspection, and the statement gives no final loss assessment.

sources.title: Wsparcie samorządów w działaniach na rzecz adaptacji do zmiany klimatu
sources.organization: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
sources.temporal_coverage: Eastern Poland municipal support project under the 2021–2027 EU programme; city adaptation plans due by 2 January 2028.
sources.methodology: Ministry page outlines the Eastern Poland adaptation project.
sources.limitations: No independent project evaluation is provided.

claims.locator: Official summary beneath the Klimat Polski 2025 report entry
claims.paraphrase: IMGW-PIB reports Poland's 2025 mean air temperature at 9.5°C, 0.8°C above the 1991–2020 normal, and annual precipitation at 89.3% of the long-term norm, classifying 2025 as dry.
claims.limitations: These are national annual averages; station-level distribution and the full report's detailed analyses were not inspected.

claims.locator: Section Polska. Kraj ocieplający się szybciej niż globalna średnia
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry states that Poland's mean annual temperature rose about 2°C since 1951, at roughly twice the global-average rate.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: The page gives no regional breakdown or temperature-trend calculation details.

claims.locator: Section Polska. Kraj ocieplający się szybciej niż globalna średnia
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry identifies March 2026 as Poland's third-warmest and third-driest March since 1951: 6.4°C mean temperature, 3.3°C above normal, and 29% of normal precipitation.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: This is a single monthly episode; the page does not attribute it to climate change.

claims.locator: Section Susza staje się problemem strukturalnym
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry reports annual water availability of 1,600 m³ per person in Poland, versus 4,500 m³ for Europe.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: No subnational distribution, seasonal profile or sector-level allocation is provided.

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry identifies Wielkopolska among Poland's most drought-affected regions, citing low rainfall, hydrology, intensive farming, low forest cover and a water balance worsening since the early 2000s.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: The page gives no quantified regional comparison or underlying hydrological series.

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry says rising temperatures, long dry spells and snowless winters worsen Wielkopolska's water balance; open-pit mining and intensive farming further deepen drought problems.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: This is a Ministry characterization, not a quantified causal analysis.

claims.locator: Sections Partnerstwo regionalne and Co zakłada porozumienie
claims.paraphrase: On 2 April 2026, the Ministry and regional partners signed a water-retention and water-security letter, joining administration, science and public bodies around catchment-scale planning.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: The letter and coordination model do not establish implementation or resilience outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry lists lake protection in Powidz Landscape Park, Ślesiński Canal modernization, Gniezno Lakeland water-resource restoration and hydrological restoration in the Warcica basin as in implementation.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: The page gives no completion dates, costs or measured water outcomes.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 26, Poland case study, Urban adaptation measures selected for the Polish cities, Bydgoszcz: Rain is profit
claims.paraphrase: Bydgoszcz's project began in 2017: 14 km new and about 90 km renovated storm sewers, six reservoirs and 22 treatment plants; target capture was about 37,000 m³.
claims.limitations: The report describes project outputs and targets but does not evaluate post-project flood outcomes.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 27–28, Poland case study, Gdańsk: drainage system
claims.paraphrase: Gdańsk invested PLN 380m in drainage and flood infrastructure during 2001–2015; storage rose over fivefold, while losses in two heavy-rain events fell from PLN 130m (2001) to PLN 10m (2016).
claims.limitations: Descriptive comparison, not controlled attribution to infrastructure.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 27–28, Poland case study, Katowice: Black to Green project
claims.paraphrase: The report describes Katowice's post-industrial adaptation features, including a green roof and planted public spaces; Bogucki Park's revitalization included a planned underground rainwater reservoir.
claims.limitations: The report says the park was undergoing revitalization and the reservoir was planned, not completed.

claims.locator: Section Losses caused by the disaster, paragraphs reporting the 21 September 2024 briefing
claims.paraphrase: At the 21 September briefing, the government reported 749 settlements under disaster state, 2.39 million residents in affected areas, 57,000 directly flood-affected residents and more than 6,544 evacuees.
geographies: flood-affected settlements under a state of natural disaster
claims.limitations: The 2.39 million figure is the population of affected areas, not the directly affected count; figures were preliminary.

claims.locator: Section Losses caused by the disaster, preliminary building-damage figures
claims.paraphrase: Preliminary reports counted 11,502 damaged residential buildings, 6,033 farm buildings and 724 public buildings; Lower Silesia alone reported damage to 54 schools.
claims.limitations: The briefing states that standing water prevented a complete inspection and that reported totals were incomplete.

claims.locator: Opening paragraph on damage estimates and the rebuilding programme
claims.paraphrase: The Prime Minister said the 2024 disaster showed a need for new flood-control infrastructure.
claims.limitations: This is a 2024 government policy judgment, not an evaluation of existing flood defenses.

claims.locator: Sections Kogo obejmie wsparcie and Projekt Wsparcie działań adaptacyjnych dla Polski Wschodniej
claims.paraphrase: The project targets medium cities and spa municipalities in Podkarpackie, Lubelskie, Świętokrzyskie, Podlaskie, Warmian-Masurian and part of Mazowieckie.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry says 58 of 75 medium Eastern Polish cities (>15,000 residents) are losing functions and municipalities have limited planning staff.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland

claims.locator: Sections Główne działania, Rezultaty and Finansowanie
claims.paraphrase: A PLN 6.27m project, including PLN 5.33m EU funds, plans municipal training, advice and peer exchange for adaptation plans.
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland

claims.paraphrase: Law requires cities of 20,000+ residents to prepare climate-adaptation plans by 2 January 2028.
affected_groups: residents of cities with at least 20,000 people
institutions: Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland
claims.limitations: The page states the statutory deadline but does not report municipal compliance.

search_audit.query: Poland Klimada 2.0 municipal climate risk vulnerability drought flood local adaptation government report
search_audit.outcome: Located an IMGW national baseline, a Ministry description of Wielkopolska drought vulnerability and projects, and city-specific measures in the World Bank's 2024 report. Statistics Poland's 2024 flood report was a lead but its landing page and PDF timed out on direct access, so its indexed text was excluded.

search_audit.query: Poland climate change conflict violence fragility climate security report resource conflict primary source
search_audit.outcome: No country-specific primary source was directly read that states a climate-to-conflict or violence mechanism for Poland. Official climate-security wording was not treated as evidence of an FCV pathway.

search_audit.query: Poland floods conflict displacement insecurity climate adaptation constraints emergency official report 2024
search_audit.outcome: The directly read 2024 flood statements describe disaster impacts and reconstruction, not conflict or insecurity constraining climate adaptation. No source-stated reverse pathway was located.

search_audit.query: Poland local climate vulnerability drought flood adaptation capacity municipal report official government regions
search_audit.outcome: Found direct Ministry accounts of Wielkopolska catchment coordination and Eastern Poland municipal capacity support, plus city-level adaptation actions described in the World Bank report. These are adaptation and administrative-capacity findings, not FCV evidence.

gaps: No direct, country-specific primary source-stated climate-to-FCV or FCV-to-adaptation pathway was found in the completed searches; this is an evidence-search gap, not evidence that no such relationship exists.
The Statistics Poland 2024 flood report could not be directly opened; search-indexed claims about local-government losses and affected population were excluded.
The 2025 IMGW report PDF exceeded the available fetch limit; its claims are limited to the directly read publisher landing-page summary.
The World Bank urban case study summarizes selected municipal projects; source adaptation plans and independent project evaluations were not inspected.
The 21 September 2024 flood impact counts are explicitly preliminary government figures, not a final damage assessment.
